definition: Yehoshua Bar-Hillel (Hebrew: יהושע בר-הלל; 8 September 1915 – 25 September 1975) was an Israeli philosopher, mathematician, and linguist.
details: He was a pioneer in the fields of machine translation and formal linguistics.

explainer.lead: Yehoshua Bar-Hillel was an Israeli philosopher, mathematician, and linguist. His work spans mathematical logic and theoretical linguistics.
explainer.knownFor: Bar-Hillel's daughter Maya Bar-Hillel is a cognitive psychologist at the Hebrew University, known for her collaborations with Amos Tversky and for her role in critiquing Bible code study.

contributions.name: He began a correspondence with Carnap in the 1940s, which led to a 1950 post-doctorate under Carnap at the University of Chicago, and to his collaborating on Carnap's 1952 An Outline of the Theory of Semantic Information.

In 1953, he founded a pioneering algebraic-computational linguistic group, and in 1961 he contributed to the proof of the pumping lemma for context-free languages (sometimes called the Bar-Hillel lemma).

timeline.what: He fought with the Haganah during the 1948 Arab–Israeli War, losing an eye.
Bar-Hillel organised the first International Conference on Machine Translation in 1952.
In 1953, Bar-Hillel joined the philosophy department at the Hebrew University, where he taught until his death at age 60.

Bar-Hillel received his PhD in Philosophy from the Hebrew University where he also studied mathematics under Abraham Fraenkel, with whom he eventually coauthored Foundations of Set Theory (1958, 1973).
